content: A flammable liquid is defined as a liquid that can ignite easily. In the United States, a flammable liquid is specifically characterized as one with a flash point below 100 degrees Fahrenheit. Liquids with a flash point between 100 degrees and 200 degrees Fahrenheit are classified as combustible liquids, which are less flammable than those in the first category. This classification system is utilized by several authoritative organizations, including the National Fire Protection Association (NFPA), the U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT), the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), and the U.S. Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA), among others. Furthermore, these categories are subdivided based on additional properties of the liquid, such as its flash point and boiling point.
